#### Purpose of this file  

This file contains all of the code for producing a curated OTU table from the 16S microbial sequence data for the Armstrong et al. manuscript entitled **"XXX"**, published by [XXX](https://doi.org/10.1093/femsec/fiaa02-AAC-9).

Here, we will process the data into a phyloseq object.

    ASV table
    Taxonomy Table
    Track Reads (metadata)

Then, we will remove the following:

    Remove Chloroplasts
    Remove Mitochondria.
    Removing ASVs from negative controls and also negative control samples.
    Evaluate accuracy by looking at the Mock Community.
    Remove samples without “enough” reads.

Finally, write data file of phyloseq output, which will be stored in Data/02-AAC--PreProcessing/phyloseq_raw_prepro.RData.

# 1 - Prepare Workspace
Load necessary R packages and set default parameters

```{r 1.1-define_paths}

# b - Define the directory containing the input data ----
  dir_in <- 
  "C:/Users/uax75/OneDrive/Documents/R/AAC-BIOcean5D-Coral_Microbiome/Data/"
    
# c - Define the directories that will contain output Files/Figures/Tables ----
```

# 2 - Import Data
Load the necessary input data

## 2.1 - Load Phyloseq Data
```{r 2-load-data}
# a - First, load the phyloseq object ----
  load(paste(dir_in,
             "01-AAC-AssignSeqVariants/",
             "01-AAC-AssignSeqVariants_physeq_raw.RData",
             sep = ""))

# b - Ceate a sample metadata table --------
  # Load the sample metadata table
  metadata <- read.xlsx(file = paste(dir_in,
                                     "01-AAC-AssignSeqVariants/",
                                     "Master_SampleKey.xlsx", sep = ""),
                        sheetName = "RData")

  # Extract the sample names from the physeq object to match to metadata
  sample.names <- colnames(otu_table(physeq_raw))
  
  # Reorganize the metadata table with the relevant data for the analysis
  samdf <- data.frame("Group" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Group"),
                      "Site" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Site"),
                      "Type" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Type"),
                      "Subtype" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Subtype"),
                      "Transplant" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Transplant"),
                      "Treatment" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Treatment"),
                      "Colony" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Colony"),
                      "Host" = vlookup(lookup_value = sample.names,
                                       dict = metadata,
                                       lookup_column = "FileName",
                                       result_column = "Species"))
  									 
  head(samdf)
  row.names(samdf) <- sample.names

# d - Append the sample metadata to the Phyloseq object ----
  sample_data(physeq_raw) <- samdf
  
  # Turn the 'treatment' column into a character vector and reorder
  sample_data(physeq_raw)$Treatment <-
    as.character(sample_data(physeq_raw)$Treatment)
  
  sample_data(physeq_raw)$Treatment <- 
    factor(sample_data(physeq_raw)$Treatment,
           levels=c("Genotype", "2-Weeks",
                    "4-Months", "Pre-HS", "Post-HS", NA))
  
  # Add a column with the SampleID names to the Phyloseq object
  sample_data(physeq_raw)['SampleID'] <- row.names(sample_data(physeq_raw)) 

```

# 3 - Data Cleanup
## 3.1 - Remove Organelle Sequences
```{r 3.1-remove_organelles}
# a - Remove Chloroplast Sequences ----

  # Make a new physeq without chloroplasts
    physeq_noChloros <-
      physeq_raw %>%
      # rm chloroplasts
      subset_taxa(Order != "Chloroplast" | is.na(Order))
  
  # How many taxa were chloroplasts? 
    num_chloro_ASVs <- ntaxa(physeq_raw) - ntaxa(physeq_noChloros)
    num_chloro_ASVs
    
# b - Remove Mitochondrial Sequences ---- 
    
  # Make a new physeq without chloroplasts
    physeq_noChlorosMitos <- 
      physeq_noChloros %>%
      subset_taxa(Family != "Mitochondria" | is.na(Family))
    
    # How many mitochondrial ASVs? 
      num_mito_ASVs <- ntaxa(physeq_noChloros) - ntaxa(physeq_noChlorosMitos)
      num_mito_ASVs
 
# c - Total number of ASVs removed from chloros and mitos 
  ntaxa(physeq_raw) - ntaxa(physeq_noChlorosMitos)
  
# d - Proportion of ASVs kept? 
  ntaxa(physeq_noChlorosMitos)/ntaxa(physeq_raw)
  
```

## 3.2 - Evaluate & Remove Controls
Inspect the negative controls, then decide which of the ASVs found in them are
genuine contaminants rather than real taxa carried into the blanks by index
hopping and low-level cross-contamination.

    Negative controls
    ASVs found within the negative controls and their distribution in the samples.
    Statistical identification of contaminants with decontam

Four negative controls carry reads - one Field Blank, one PCR Blank and two
Extraction Blanks. (A fifth control in the sample key yielded none, and script 01
drops `neg-pcr2` as a bad sample.)

This step changed on 27 October 2026. Two faults had to be corrected together:
`ASVs_control` was built as a one-column data.frame rather than a character
vector, so the removal in step i matched nothing and no ASV was ever discarded;
and until the environmental and control FASTQs were re-trimmed to the common
amplicon window (see section 3.2 of script 01), no blank ASV could have matched a
coral ASV in any case, because the two sets of reads began at different bases.
With both repaired, the blanks share an ASV space with the samples for the first
time and this filter finally has real work to do - which is also why blanket
removal of every blank ASV is no longer acceptable and decontam is used instead.

```{r 3.2-remove_controls}
# a - Create a vector of samples that were negative controls --
  samples_control <- 
  rownames(subset(sample_data(physeq_raw), 
                   Subtype %in% 
                     c("PCR Blank", "Extraction Blank", "Field Blank")))

# b - Make a new phyloseq object of only the control samples ----
  physeq_control <- 
    physeq_noChlorosMitos %>%
    prune_samples(
      (sample_names(physeq_noChlorosMitos) %in% samples_control), .) %>%
    #subset_samples(., names %in% samples_control) %>%
    # force remove ASVs with 0 counts 
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(.) > 0, .)

  physeq_control
  
# c - Control ASVs, in both identifier namespaces ----
  # NOTE: as.vector() does NOT flatten a data.frame - it returns it unchanged -
  # so the previous version of this object was a one-column data.frame. Step e
  # worked because it indexed ASVs_control$ASV, but step i tested
  # `ASV %in% ASVs_control` against the data.frame itself, which coerces to a
  # deparsed string, matches nothing, and silently removed no taxa at all.
  # dplyr::pull() returns the character vector both steps assume.
  ASVs_control <- 
    physeq_control %>%
    tax_table() %>%
    data.frame() %>%
    dplyr::pull(ASV)

  # This object carries the tax_table's ASV column ("ASV_1", "ASV_2", ...),
  # which is NOT the same namespace as taxa_names(): script 01 renames taxa via
  # microbiome::add_refseq(tag = "ASV") to "ASV1", "ASV2", .... Pruning must use
  # taxa_names(), so keep a matching vector in that namespace and never mix them.
  seqs_control <- taxa_names(physeq_control)

  stopifnot(length(ASVs_control) == length(seqs_control))

# c2 - Cap the set used for plotting and testing ----
  # Steps d-h draw one facet panel and one Wilcoxon test per blank ASV. Before
  # the amplicon window was repaired the blanks shared almost nothing with the
  # samples, so that was a handful of panels; now that they occupy the same ASV
  # space it can be hundreds, which makes the figure unreadable and risks
  # stat_pvalue_manual() failing on NA positions from constant-value groups.
  # The diagnostic is therefore capped at the most abundant blank ASVs, ranked
  # by their abundance IN THE CONTROLS - the ones that actually characterise the
  # blanks. Removal in steps i-k still considers every ASV, so nothing is
  # excluded from the filtering itself; this cap is presentational only.
  n_plot_control_asvs <- 20

  seqs_control_top <- 
    physeq_control %>%
    taxa_sums() %>%
    sort(decreasing = TRUE) %>%
    names() %>%
    head(n_plot_control_asvs)

  cat("Blank ASVs:", length(seqs_control), "total;",
      length(seqs_control_top), "shown in the diagnostic plots.\n")

# d - Visualize raw abundance values of control ASVs ----
  plot_bar(prune_taxa(seqs_control_top, physeq_control), 
           "ASV", fill = "ASV") +
    labs(title = paste0("Top ", length(seqs_control_top), 
                        " ASVs in the negative controls")) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
# e - Use vector to subset from larger dataset ---- 
  # prune_taxa() rather than subset_taxa(ASV %in% ...) so this stays in the
  # taxa_names() namespace and cannot be crossed with the tax_table ASV column.
  physeq_neg_controlASV <- 
    physeq_noChlorosMitos %>%
    prune_taxa(seqs_control_top, .) %>%
    # we will also need to remove the positive controls from the samples! 
    # We will evaluate the Mock community a bit later on. :) 
    subset_samples(., Subtype != "ZymoMock")
  
  physeq_neg_controlASV
  
# f - Plot Abundances of neg control ASVs in samples versus controls ----
  plot_bar(physeq_neg_controlASV, "ASV", facet_grid = Group~.) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
  
# g - Calculate the phylum relative abundance 
  # Note: The read depth MUST be normalized in some way: scale_reads
  asv_negControls_df <- 
    physeq_neg_controlASV %>%
    # agglomerate at the ASV level 
    tax_glom(taxrank = "ASV") %>% 
    # Melt to a long format 
    psmelt()
  
  # Set levels of Group variable so that "Control" comes first
  asv_negControls_df$Group <- factor(asv_negControls_df$Group, 
                                     levels = c("Control", "TrueSample"))
  
  # Check
  head(asv_negControls_df)
  
# h - Statistically test! 
  library(rstatix)
  negControl_ASV_statTest <- 
    asv_negControls_df %>%
    group_by(ASV) %>%
    wilcox_test(Abundance ~ Group) %>%
    # Add the x and y positions for plotting 
    adjust_pvalue(method = "fdr") %>%
    # Make the significance values be stars for plotting
    add_significance() %>%
    # Calculate where to place it on the facet grid plot
    add_xy_position(x = "Group", fun = "max", scales = "free") %>%
    # bring the pvalues a lil lower
    mutate(y.position = y.position * 0.82)
  
  ## Using ggpubr 
  ggboxplot(
    asv_negControls_df, 
    x = "Group", y = "Abundance", 
    color = "Group",
    facet.by = "ASV", scales = "free_y",add = "jitter") + 
    stat_pvalue_manual(negControl_ASV_statTest) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = c("firebrick3", "cornflowerblue")) + 
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("firebrick3", "cornflowerblue")) + 
    theme_bw() + 
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_blank(),
          legend.title = element_blank(), legend.position = c(0.85, 0.07))
  
# i - Identify contaminants with decontam ----
  # Removing every ASV that appears in a blank is too blunt. The controls share
  # the 515F/926R window with the corals, so index hopping and low-level
  # carry-over place genuine, abundant taxa in the blanks; blanket removal would
  # delete real community members. decontam's prevalence model asks the right
  # question instead - is this ASV MORE prevalent in the controls than in the
  # true samples? - and flags only those.
  #
  # threshold = 0.5 implements the "more prevalent in controls than in samples"
  # rule. It is the appropriate choice here because only four negative controls
  # carry reads (one Field, one PCR, two Extraction blanks; the fifth control in
  # the sample key yielded none), which leaves the default threshold of 0.1 with
  # very little power.

  sample_data(physeq_noChlorosMitos)$is_control <- 
    sample_data(physeq_noChlorosMitos)$Group == "Control"

  contam_df <- 
    decontam::isContaminant(physeq_noChlorosMitos,
                            method    = "prevalence",
                            neg       = "is_control",
                            threshold = 0.5)

  seqs_contaminant <- rownames(contam_df)[contam_df$contaminant]

# j - Report what is removed, against what blanket removal would have done ----
  physeq_true <- 
    physeq_noChlorosMitos %>%
    subset_samples(., Group == "TrueSample") %>%
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(.) > 0, .)

  pct_reads <- function(ps, taxa) {
    keep <- intersect(taxa_names(ps), taxa)
    if (length(keep) == 0) return(0)
    100 * sum(otu_table(prune_taxa(keep, ps))) / sum(otu_table(ps))
  }

  cat("\n--- Control filtering ---\n",
      "ASVs detected in the blanks   :", length(seqs_control),
      sprintf("(%.2f%% of true-sample reads)", pct_reads(physeq_true, seqs_control)), "\n",
      "ASVs flagged by decontam      :", length(seqs_contaminant),
      sprintf("(%.2f%% of true-sample reads)", pct_reads(physeq_true, seqs_contaminant)), "\n",
      "Blank ASVs retained as real   :", 
      length(setdiff(seqs_control, seqs_contaminant)), "\n\n")

  # Taxonomy of what is being discarded, for the record
  if (length(seqs_contaminant) > 0) {
    physeq_noChlorosMitos %>%
      prune_taxa(seqs_contaminant, .) %>%
      tax_table() %>%
      data.frame() %>%
      dplyr::select(Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, ASV) %>%
      print()
  }

# k - Remove contaminant taxa and the control samples ----
  keep_taxa <- setdiff(taxa_names(physeq_noChlorosMitos), seqs_contaminant)

  physeq_noControlsChlorosMitos <- 
    physeq_noChlorosMitos %>%
    prune_taxa(keep_taxa, .) %>%
    # Remove control samples 
    subset_samples(., !(Subtype %in% 
                          c("PCR Blank", "Extraction Blank", "Field Blank"))) %>%
    # Drop ASVs left at zero once the controls are gone
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(.) > 0, .)

  physeq_noControlsChlorosMitos

  
# j - save processed physeq object ----
  save(physeq_noControlsChlorosMitos,
         file = paste(dir_out_dat,
                      pref_out,
                      "physeq_noControlsChlorosMitos.RData", sep = ""))
```
